notes: Round 10 runs several tracks at once, each in its own worktree: M1 (land animals), M2 (water mobs), M3 (night mobs) and W's w3 (the game events W's first merge left out). D0's d0b (silverfish in stone, endermites from pearls, flying navigation) is merged (c0366f3a), and release 6 is built with PROTOCOL 11 (789f6d23). Never bump minecraft_net::PROTOCOL: the release step bumps it once when messages changed; if a commit changes a ToClient/ToServer message or the codec, add a line under '## Protocol' in the track log. Insert new match arms and list entries next to related ones, not at the end of lists, to keep merges small (E3-0 names the few positional lists that are appended). Record decisions in the track log. LOAD: builds run at -j 4 per slot to keep the laptop cool; never start a second cargo command, the game, or any other long CPU-heavy process. Keep to the brief: each section names the commit its file:line anchors come from, so re-check every anchor before editing; keep off the hooks the M briefs own and follow the cross-area overlaps (both in E3-0). E2's e2b (44d96765) and D0's d0b (c0366f3a) are merged, so every 'waits for e2b', 'after d0b' and 'release 6 built' in the brief is met; d0b moved lines in server.rs, world.rs, walk_path.rs, entity_view.rs and families.rs, so anchors taken before it need a re-check. The orchestrator brings track-e3 up to minecraft-survival before each segment, so the review uses git diff r10-e3m-base..HEAD as usual. SEGMENT e3m: E3-11's first three mob groups: age locks and Silent, fireballs and wind charges blaming the right one, floating in thin water and jump boost on mobs.

Track E3 group mob-floats-jumps: build track-e3.md section E3-11 group mob-floats-jumps. Commits: (1) 'Minecraft silverfish, endermites, cats and baby animals float in thin water like vanilla', (2) 'Minecraft mobs take jump boost from potions and tipped arrows like vanilla', (3) 'Minecraft breezes leap higher with jump boost'. Key points: (1) fluid.rs gets pub fn jump_threshold(eye_height) -> f64 after floatable_height (:50); it is vanilla's Entity.getFluidJumpThreshold (eye below 0.4 gives 0, else 0.4). Every FloatGoal uses it with its eye height: monster_ai.rs:2064, chicken_ai.rs:100, cow_ai.rs:177, pig_ai.rs:309, eat_block.rs:109. Pass the same threshold to living_jump at world.rs:1088 (leave M1's :1064 panda line alone), wolves.rs:181 and felines.rs:265. wolves.rs tick_ai sets ai.state.eye_height = eye after :130, so a puppy's goals see the baby eye. (2) MobEffect::JumpBoost goes after SlowFalling (enum, ALL now 17, id minecraft:jump_boost). Body.jump_boost: Option<u8> goes next to levitation and slow_falling (movement.rs:77, :116); float_from sets it. Body::jump_power (:642) adds 0.1*(amplifier+1), and living_jump's power line (:263) calls jump_power(world, 0.42, 1.0), which covers ridden horses, ravagers and rabbits. living::fall_damage uses safe distance 3 + (amplifier+1). The horse's own fall (horse_fall in M3's world/equines.rs, which M3's camels reuse) and the registry's generic landing in families.rs (a shared root site) keep 3: log both as left for M3 and the registry's owner. Potions and saves pick it up through MobEffect::from_id. (3) breeze Ctx gets jump_boost: f32 next to levitating (:107), filled at breezes.rs:242 (test literal :852). tick_long_jump adds normalize().y * jump_boost to the leap. Stay off M2's movement.rs lines (travel_swimming, move_self) and M3's travel_water_slowed. Tests are listed in the section. End with the owner's steps and the kit line.
